# Base image with Flux, OpenMPI, and EFA support for ARM on AWS Kubernetes
# This provides a pre-configured environment for multi-node MPI communication.
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set environment variables for the build
ENV OSU_BENCHMARKS_VERSION=7.3
ENV OSU_BENCHMARKS_URL=http://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/download/mvapich/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_BENCHMARKS_VERSION}.tar.gz

# Set the C and C++ compilers to the MPI wrappers provided by the base image.
# This ensures that the OSU Benchmarks are compiled with MPI support.
ENV CC=mpicc
ENV CXX=mpicxx

# Perform system updates, install dependencies, download, build,
# install benchmarks, and clean up all in a single RUN command to minimize layer size.
RUN set -e && \
    # Update package lists and install build dependencies and certificates.
    # --no-install-recommends reduces unnecessary package installation.
    apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    wget \
    automake \
    autoconf \
    libtool \
    ca-certificates && \
    \
    # Create a temporary directory for the build process.
    mkdir -p /tmp/build && \
    cd /tmp/build && \
    \
    # Download the OSU Benchmarks source code and extract it.
    # The --strip-components=1 flag removes the top-level directory from the tarball.
    wget -q -O - ${OSU_BENCHMARKS_URL} | tar -xz --strip-components=1 && \
    \
    # Configure the build. The build system will automatically use the
    # compilers specified by the CC and CXX environment variables.
    ./configure && \
    \
    # Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # Find all compiled MPI benchmark executables and copy them to /usr/local/bin,
    # which is in the default system PATH. This makes benchmarks like 'osu_latency'
    # directly available to the user.
    find ./c/mpi -type f -name "osu_*" -executable -exec cp {} /usr/local/bin/ \; && \
    \
    # Clean up to reduce the final image size.
    # Remove the build directory and the apt package cache.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# The container is now ready. The OSU benchmark executables (e.g., osu_latency)
# can be run directly with mpirun or flux.
# Example: mpirun -np 2 osu_latency

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the OSU latency benchmark
# across two nodes in an AWS Kubernetes environment using ARM-based CPU instances
# with Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for high-performance networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job
  name: osu-latency-arm-aws
  # Deployment will be in the 'default' namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Number of pods in the MiniCluster, corresponding to the number of nodes for this test
  size: 2
  # Total number of MPI tasks. For a point-to-point latency test, 2 tasks are needed.
  tasks: 2

  # Do not delete pods after the job finishes to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging mode for detailed output from the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Define pod-level specifications, such as resource requests for special hardware.
  pod:
    resources:
      # Request and limit one EFA device per pod. This is crucial for high-performance,
      # low-latency internode communication on AWS.
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

  # Flux-specific configuration section
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture of the nodes, which is ARM for this use case.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use an ARM-compatible Flux view image, as required for ARM instances.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disabling the separate Flux container injects flux directly into the application container.
      # This is a common pattern for performance-sensitive applications.
      disable: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:osu-latency
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # 'osu_latency' is the executable for the OSU Point-to-Point Latency test.
      command: osu_latency
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is used for the experiment.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # This container runs the application workload, it is not the lead broker/launcher.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest runs the OSU latency benchmark on AWS ARM
# instances, incorporating fixes for resource allocation and adding pod scheduling specifics.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job
  name: osu-latency-arm-aws
  # Deployment will be in the 'default' namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, corresponding to the two nodes for the test.
  size: 2
  # The total number of MPI tasks. For a point-to-point latency test, 2 tasks are required.
  tasks: 2

  # Limit job retries to 1 on failure to prevent excessive restarts.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Do not delete pods after the job finishes to allow for log inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging mode for detailed output from the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod-level specifications, including scheduling and restart behavior.
  pod:
    # Ensure pods are scheduled on specific AWS ARM instances for this experiment.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
    # Prevent Kubernetes from restarting the pod on failure, preserving logs for debugging.
    restartPolicy: Never

  # Flux-specific configuration section.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture of the nodes is ARM.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use an ARM-compatible Flux view image.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disable the separate Flux container to inject Flux directly into the application container for performance.
      disable: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:osu-latency
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # 'osu_latency' is the executable for the OSU Point-to-Point Latency test.
      command: osu_latency
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is used for the experiment.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # This container runs the application workload; it is not the lead broker/launcher.
      launcher: false
      # CORRECTED: Resource requests and limits must be defined at the container level.
      # This requests one Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) device per pod for high-performance networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Build the OSU benchmarks. You MUST have MPI support enabled. You MUST ensure osu_latency is on the path.
You MUST build for a multi-node MPI environment

context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3).
context.details:
Run The OSU Latency benchmark across 2 nodes.
You MUST run on 2 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
